record_notes.DCP-LETT-372: Answers an unlocated Mrs Horner note postponing tomorrow visit; proposes Monday. Cake received from Shrewsbury this morning is a parcel event, not proof of any enclosed letter. Later Leonard note408 is a different sender and event.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-408: Leonard Horner postpones Monday visit for Factory Act business. Later use of blank pages for marriage notes does not date Darwin receipt or create response prose.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-436: Charlotte congratulations with no confirming news in that day post. Expected further letters are not received knowledge. No Darwin response located.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-450: Charlotte thanks for a Darwin letter received on same day as an Emma letter. The Darwin input is unlocated; incoming-only voice.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-453: Official council response to unlocated Jukes application, containing reference to Governor Prescott extract. A collective decision conveyed by Darwin, not a surviving incoming pair.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-461: Reports unlocated Sedgwick letter and council discussion, offers Jukes surveying advice. 453 is an earlier Darwin outgoing, not this reply input.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-520: Fitton thanks for book and discusses its tone and geological content. No surviving covering letter found; book reading by Fitton does not establish Darwin receipt.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-546: Proposes Miller reduce Sulivan weather observations covering October-March. The dataset and calibration discussion exceed429, which covers only the opening days, so429 is not uniquely identified as this source.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-548C: Darwin testimonial for John Edward Gray, not George Robert Gray. Copied signature does not establish joint authorship; no request letter located.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-550: Atlas and Sulphur Island coordinate reply; incoming Hall enquiry unlocated. Do not confuse with later Coquimbo discussion558F.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-558F: Answers unlocated Hall query about terraces; earlier conversation with Lyell and published works are distinct sources. Several private communications about Scottish parallel roads are mentioned without identifying any single one.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-607: Published letter about bees, responding to public Gardeners Chronicle discussion rather than a private incoming letter. Header date is draft August16; displayed published text appeared August21. Keep source-form date distinction and mark exact text dating for review.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-632: Excerpt of Darwin letter to Fitton, later copied to Buckland and Agassiz. Grateful for Buckland published abstract, not a Buckland incoming letter. Earlier misidentification as Dr Tritten is editorially corrected.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-648: Thanks Mrs Horner for unlocated congratulations and tells her of Lyell flattering coral-volume letter. No surviving Lyell incoming in1842 exists in this corpus; do not backfill with343/376/425/604/670.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-650: Answers unlocated Jackson review proposal and mentions same missing Lyell coral criticism. Review intended for Journal or periodical is not yet published knowledge.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-651: Asks Miller to locate old rock specimens; cites earlier notes and future special meeting. December3 is Darwin stated plan while records give actual December2; no need to rewrite the letter date. Broad Sunday interval retained.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-662: Printed response to Maclaren published review, with an unlocated Lyell note received around composition. Public review is outside private incoming corpus; original November-December1842 writing interval retained despite January1843 publication.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-660F: Requests museum loan of coral specimens for Lyell future lectures. Request and earlier donation/accession are distinct events; Gray reverse draft is not Darwin voice.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-661: Short postscript on annotated Maclaren reprint. February1843 depends on editorial inference from omitted corrections, not exact day. Preserve annotations separately; no missing letter reconstructed.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-671: Hinds answers Darwin unlocated April9 letter; cautious evidence on coral, islands and birds. This is incoming voice and date of writing, not Darwin receipt.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-672: Declines proposed RGS Council listing because travel costs time. Jackson invitation unlocated; do not pair with earlier outgoing568 accepting different-year appointment.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-677: Catalogue explicitly warns this could be a corrupted copy with interpolations or a forgery. Unused address and Hooker salutation conflict with metadata Horner. Quarantine all prose from Darwin voice; raw date and source preserved.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-683: Hinds reports newly examined Cactornis after a missing Darwin note. Shared subject with671 establishes continuity, not a reply between two incoming letters. Later correction of habitat is not injected into1843 knowledge.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-693: Published botanical letter and postscript about double flowers and cabbage leaf. Lindley editorial replies are excluded from body extraction and remain editorial context. Plant observation dates differ from late-August composition.
